about.title: About HealthCalc
about.meta_desc: Learn about HealthCalc, our mission to provide free, science-backed health calculators, and the formulas we use.
about.mission_content: HealthCalc was created with a simple goal: to provide everyone with free, accessible, and scientifically accurate health calculation tools. We believe that understanding your body's basic metrics—like Body Mass Index (BMI), Basal Metabolic Rate (BMR), and Total Daily Energy Expenditure (TDEE)—should be straightforward and available to all, without registration, paywalls, or unnecessary complexity.
about.mission_content2: Our calculators are designed to help you make informed decisions about your health and fitness goals. Whether you're trying to lose weight, gain muscle, maintain your current physique, or simply understand your body better, our tools provide the foundational metrics you need.
about.formulas_intro: All of our calculators are built on validated scientific formulas and international health standards:
about.bmi_info_content: Our BMI (Body Mass Index) calculator uses the standard formula adopted by the World Health Organization (WHO). BMI is calculated by dividing your weight in kilograms by the square of your height in meters. The classification categories (underweight, normal weight, overweight, obese) follow WHO guidelines, which are recognized internationally as screening tools for weight-related health risks.
about.bmr_info_content: Our BMR (Basal Metabolic Rate) calculator implements the Mifflin-St Jeor equation, which is considered one of the most accurate formulas for estimating resting energy expenditure. This equation was developed through extensive research and has been validated across diverse populations. It accounts for your weight, height, age, and biological sex to estimate the number of calories your body burns at complete rest.
about.tdee_info_content: Our TDEE (Total Daily Energy Expenditure) calculator builds upon your BMR by applying the Harris-Benedict activity multipliers. These multipliers account for different levels of physical activity, from sedentary lifestyles to very active routines. The result tells you approximately how many calories you burn per day, including all activities, which is essential for planning dietary needs for weight loss, maintenance, or gain.
about.commitment_privacy: Privacy First: All calculations are performed entirely in your web browser. We do not collect, store, or transmit your personal health data. Your information never leaves your device.
about.commitment_no_registration: No Registration Required: Use all our calculators instantly without creating an account, providing an email address, or sharing any personal information.
about.commitment_free: Completely Free: Our tools are free to use, now and always. We believe health information should be accessible to everyone.
about.commitment_ads: Ad-Supported: To keep our service free, we display ads through Google AdSense. We carefully balance monetization with user experience, ensuring ads don't interfere with the functionality of our calculators.
about.improvement_content: We are committed to maintaining and improving HealthCalc. We regularly review the latest research in health and nutrition science to ensure our calculators remain accurate and up-to-date. User feedback helps us identify areas for improvement and new features that would benefit our community.
about.medical_disclaimer_content: The calculators and information provided on HealthCalc are for educational and informational purposes only. They are not intended to replace, substitute for, or serve as professional medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment.
about.medical_disclaimer_consult: Always consult with a qualified healthcare provider before:
about.medical_disclaimer_diet: Starting any new diet or exercise program
about.medical_disclaimer_changes: Making significant changes to your eating habits
about.medical_disclaimer_weight: Using these metrics to guide weight loss or gain strategies
about.medical_disclaimer_conditions: If you have any medical conditions or concerns
about.medical_disclaimer_footer: Individual health needs vary significantly, and a healthcare professional can provide personalized advice based on your complete medical history, current health status, and specific circumstances. Never disregard professional medical advice or delay seeking it because of information obtained from this website.

how_it_works.section_title: How It Works: Understanding Your Health Metrics
how_it_works.what_is_bmi_content: Body Mass Index (BMI) is a screening tool that estimates whether your weight falls within a healthy range relative to your height. Calculated by dividing your weight in kilograms by the square of your height in meters, BMI provides a quick assessment of potential health risks associated with being underweight, overweight, or obese. While BMI doesn't measure body fat directly or account for muscle mass, it serves as a useful starting point for evaluating weight-related health concerns. The World Health Organization categorizes BMI values into ranges: underweight (below 18.5), normal weight (18.5-24.9), overweight (25-29.9), and obese (30 and above). These categories help identify individuals who may benefit from consulting healthcare providers about their weight.
how_it_works.what_is_bmr_content: Basal Metabolic Rate (BMR) represents the minimum number of calories your body needs to maintain basic physiological functions while at complete rest. This includes breathing, circulation, cell production, nutrient processing, and temperature regulation. Your BMR accounts for approximately 60-75% of your total daily energy expenditure and is influenced by factors including your weight, height, age, and biological sex. Understanding your BMR is crucial because it establishes the baseline caloric needs your body requires just to stay alive. Our calculator uses the scientifically validated Mifflin-St Jeor equation, which has been proven accurate across diverse populations. Knowing your BMR helps you make informed decisions about caloric intake, whether your goal is weight loss, maintenance, or gain.
how_it_works.what_is_tdee: What is TDEE (Total Daily Energy Expenditure)?
how_it_works.what_is_tdee_content: Total Daily Energy Expenditure (TDEE) estimates the total number of calories you burn in a full 24-hour period, including all physical activities. While BMR covers only resting metabolism, TDEE accounts for everything: walking, working, exercising, digesting food, and even fidgeting. TDEE is calculated by multiplying your BMR by an activity factor that corresponds to your lifestyle—ranging from sedentary (little to no exercise) to very active (intense exercise 6-7 days per week). This metric is essential for planning your nutrition because it tells you how many calories you need to consume to maintain your current weight. To lose weight, you'd eat below your TDEE; to gain weight, you'd eat above it; and to maintain, you'd match it.
how_it_works.why_matters: Why These Metrics Matter for Your Health
how_it_works.why_matters_content: Understanding your BMI, BMR, and TDEE empowers you to take control of your health journey with data-driven insights. BMI helps you assess whether your current weight may pose health risks and whether you should consult a healthcare provider. BMR reveals the minimum energy your body requires, preventing dangerously low caloric intake that can slow metabolism and harm health. TDEE provides the complete picture of your energy needs, enabling you to create realistic and sustainable nutrition plans aligned with your goals. Together, these three metrics form a comprehensive framework for understanding your body's needs and making informed decisions about diet and exercise.
how_it_works.using_together_content: For the most effective use of HealthCalc, we recommend using all three calculators in sequence. Start with the BMI calculator to understand your current weight status and identify if weight management should be a priority. Next, calculate your BMR to learn your baseline caloric needs—this ensures you never cut calories too drastically, which can be counterproductive and unhealthy. Finally, use the TDEE calculator to determine your total daily caloric needs based on your activity level. With these three numbers, you can create a personalized nutrition plan: subtract 300-500 calories from your TDEE for gradual weight loss, add 300-500 for weight gain, or match it for maintenance. All calculations are performed locally in your browser, ensuring complete privacy—your health data never leaves your device.
